server_instructions:
## MCP Server Instructions
### tatc
Use the satellite search tool when a satellite name is broad or ambiguous. Use the satellite info tool for metadata and current GP (OMM) elements. Use the ground-track tool only after resolving an exact satellite name or NORAD ID; its times are UTC and its position altitude is in meters. Use the instrument search tool to find sensors by name, acronym, or type. Use the satellite-instruments tool when you need to compare the payloads on a satellite. Use the instrument info tool for an instrument's measurement specs and carrying satellites; its spec values are source text, not parsed numbers. The geometry resolver returns source context and numeric candidates; it does not assess compatibility. Read the complete instrument context, identify the source value and mode for this study, and assess whether the coverage model represents that geometry. Mark geometry supported only when the source evidence establishes continuous nadir-centered coverage without gaps or separate pointing. For separated tracks with a documented overall span, use that span only as an approximate filled envelope and warn that gaps count as accessible in the model. Do not present it as continuous coverage. For any known mismatch, provide status approximate and a specific warning about what the model simplifies. Approximate runs automatically without confirmation, and the warning remains with summaries and fetched views. Before any run, ask the researcher to resolve an applicable mode or value left unclear by the source, insufficient evidence, or conflicting source facts. Never choose a typical, widest, or best-case option for the researcher. Keep source_text faithful to returned evidence; never add a selected value or mode to make it appear sourced. Supply a geometry_assessment with relevant source_text and an explanation to the finish tool. Its checks validate the structure and numeric value, not the scientific interpretation or source authenticity. A citation alone is not evidence. Do not fetch arbitrary reference URLs. For a legacy run, a researcher-supplied synthetic study excerpt is valid evidence for that study assumption. Do not mark a legacy run approximate only because the excerpt is synthetic or because the real instrument is more complex. Mark it approximate when the excerpt itself documents a gap, separate pointing, or another mismatch with the continuous model, or when the researcher's explicit assumption leaves that mismatch unresolved. The conical source-conflict and approximation rules apply only to conical preparation; they do not relabel a legacy geometry assessment. For coverage, call the begin tool, then the region tool, then the finish tool, then the fetch tools by result ID for daily rows, coverage cells as GeoJSON, or revisit numbers. The begin tool takes several satellites separated by commas to model a constellation. Set daylight_only on the finish tool for optical imagers. For a conical scanner, use the separate conical preparation and finish workflow instead of legacy field_of_regard_deg or swath_width_km. First use the shared configuration lookup tool to inspect matching revisions. It returns candidates but does not select one. Pass the researcher's explicit configuration_id and revision to preparation; never choose the latest revision implicitly. A researcher may instead supply one complete study-specific sourced conical configuration. The configuration: identity, spacecraft and orbit-provider identity, mode, channel, applicability interval, typed angles with units and frames, evidence excerpts with locators, source revision, interpretation, source conflicts and chosen rationale, reported geometry checks, approximation status, and approximations. Never invent cone angles, sector widths, dates, or evidence. A nominal swath or ground incidence angle does not establish the cone/sector mapping. The conical preparation tool returns the region, grid, window, consequential settings, conflicts, approximations, warnings, and a setup revision, but runs no calculation. Show those choices to the researcher and obtain their acceptance; only then call the conical finish tool with that exact setup revision and accept_setup=true. Never set accept_setup true without the researcher's acceptance. If region, grid, window, orbit, configuration, source choice, approximation, or software changed, prepare again for a new revision. The finish tool rejects stale revisions and runs no calculation for them. Use the instrument configuration refresh tool only when the assistant or maintainer has checked source evidence. It records unchanged, documentation-only, changed-geometry, changed-applicability, or failed checks. A documentation-only change adds a review notice without a new revision. A geometry or applicability change creates a separate selectable immutable revision and a notice on the prior one. A failed check means the source status is unknown. The server intersects established applicability with the requested window. Dates it cannot establish are unresolved, not zero access. The single-configuration conical and pointed workflows prepare a partial-date proposal when part of the window is unresolved, and require acceptance before running. An explicit applicability_assumption may extend a configuration only when the proposed setup records its rationale and the researcher accepts the revised setup; a result modeled under assumptions is not independently established. Conical results preserve each valid TAT-C viewing epoch. The broader field-of-regard period is envelope metadata only: never describe it as continuous viewing, access duration, or uncovered duration. Daily area counts a cell once per half-open UTC day when an event epoch falls in that day. Cell-center sampling does not mean an entire cell was viewed. Event spacing is null with fewer than two distinct events at a cell. Use the viewing-event fetch tool for paged epochs, the event-spacing fetch tool for paged per-cell spacing, and the usual daily, cell, and revisit fetches for the other views. Preparation, finish, and paged fetches carry the accepted setup revision, configuration digest, and a snapshot reference; use the study setup getter with the draft or result ID to retrieve the full configuration, evidence excerpts, rationales, warnings, and definitions. A study may set orbit_direction to ascending or descending per configuration; the filter keeps only events whose TAT-C propagated latitude is increasing or decreasing at the event epoch. State that filter and its events excluded. Use the study export tool with a saved result ID when the researcher wants a durable file. The download link is valid for 15 minutes and the JSON file contains the exact orbit records, accepted setup, software versions, assumptions, results, and a replay block. Results and drafts expire after 24 hours and can be lost earlier on restart or capacity eviction. Study-specific settings are not promoted to a shared registry. For a side-looking radar, use the pointed preparation and finish workflow. Inspect the spacecraft-specific registry record, choose an exact revision, and keep off-nadir look angles separate from ground incidence angles. Preserve look direction, velocity and nadir frames, roll and pitch assumptions, applicability, subswath ranges by altitude, evidence, measured residuals, tolerances, and approximation warnings. A limited pointed record requires researcher acceptance and does not establish an acquisition schedule or mission capability. Use its pointed event, daily, cell, and revisit fetches. Field-of-regard envelopes remain metadata; count access only at valid TAT-C event epochs. For more than one selected configuration, use the mixed study preparation tool and mixed study finish tool. It accepts one to six exact registry revisions or complete study-specific configurations, across at most six spacecraft. Add orbit_direction to an individual selection to keep only its ascending or descending passes; each configuration can use a different direction. Every staged spacecraft must have a selected configuration or recorded omission. Established applicability is intersected with the window; unresolved dates remain explicit and make the result partial. When a requested instrument cannot be modeled, prepare a partial proposal with omissions: name the instrument and spacecraft, choose a reason_code, give the reason, and attach evidence when a source conflict or missing evidence caused it. Use awaiting_clarification plus the question when a choice is still open. A partial proposal needs at least one calculable configuration; never turn an all-unresolved request into a zero-coverage study. Finish a partial proposal only with accepted_omissions set to exactly the returned omission IDs. Report completeness_status partial, name every omitted instrument and its reason, and say its access is unknown; never report an omission as zero events. A modeled configuration with zero valid events is a modeled zero over its interval, not an omission. If a calculation fails after acceptance, name the failed configuration, save nothing, and prepare a newly accepted proposal before dropping it. Keep each configuration's identity, source revision, orbit, geometry, and illumination setting separate. A target-sunlit filter may be a study assumption; report its note and do not call it a source-established scientific requirement. TAT-C applies each configuration's filter independently, including for configurations sharing a spacecraft. Mixed fetches return the combined cell-union scope when configuration_id is omitted, or one configuration's contribution when its exact ID is supplied. Exact simultaneous events retain all contributors and count once for combined spacing; nearby epochs remain separate. Combined daily area counts each visited cell ID once. Keep the setup provenance, warnings, completeness status, and accounting definitions with every view. Coverage is modeled access at each grid-cell center only: never claim every point of the region was scanned or that an acquisition occurred. A daily gap_area_km2 of 0 means every cell center had access that UTC day, not continuous observation. Talk to the researcher like a companion, in plain sentences with every number that matters: the geometry value and its source, the metrics, the window. Show the result ID once, since follow-up questions need it. Never show draft IDs, function names, call syntax, or raw payloads, and never narrate your tool steps. Ask for missing pieces conversationally, like a place and dates. When the user asks to visualize, map, plot, or show a ground track, use the ground track map tool with the satellite, start time, duration, and step interval you would give the ground-track tool. It opens the Cesium Study pane. A satellite-only ground track has no sensor coverage. Supply an instrument only when the researcher supplied or agreed to its geometry; never assume a cone. All tools are read-only. Never write tool-call syntax such as <function=...> in a reply; call the tool or answer in prose. Ground-track requests and regional studies keep the workflows above. Everything after this sentence applies only to the point-coverage explorer: the coverage analysis and research visualization tools. Point coverage studies of mission designs the user supplies (satellite orbits, instruments, and named study locations) use the coverage analysis tool for numbers and the research visualization tool for the study pane. Choose the explorer's presentation from the research question and conversation context, not trigger words: it can be a chart, a table, a timeline, a geographic map, or an orbital simulation, not always a Cesium scene. Ask a focused question only when missing inputs or competing interpretations would materially change the study. Do not ask the user to write tool names or special prompt syntax. Use the research visualization tool when a visual or interactive point study is requested or clearly implied: coverage comparisons as overview charts, access/gap timing as timelines, exact values as tables, geography as map2d, and orbital motion or spatial geometry as simulation3d. The data view renders values from an earlier analysis or supplied dataset without rerunning physics. The orbit view can also show altitude charts and sampled-position tables without loading a globe. Informational questions, TLE text, requests to write plotting code, and numerical answers do not automatically request an interactive scene. Preserve a point study's requested time windows and scope; explain its limits and ask before shortening or reducing inputs. A point coverage study requires satellites, instruments and study locations supplied or agreed in this conversation. An orbit alone is not sensor coverage. Use the built-in example only when the user requests an example. Answer follow-up questions about an earlier study from the exact values in its tool result, and re-show it in another presentation with the visualize call that result states; never rebuild it from memory. For UI-originated rerun_tatc_study intents, call the registered visualization tool using the exact params provided, preserving workspace_id so the study pane receives the new result. Do not substitute the example. Coverage gaps at the window boundaries are not complete revisits; interpolated display samples are not the event analysis resolution. A point study evaluates only the supplied points, not the area between them. A point study with a pointed or conical instrument counts only valid viewing epochs: its field-of-regard envelopes are not viewing time, and its time covered, gaps and revisit are unavailable, not zero. In a point study, use only values the user supplied or tools returned in this conversation; never invent satellites, TLEs, orbits, sensor field of regard, locations, dates or metrics. Place names such as Phoenix are study points or ground stations, not satellites. The study pane draws supplied basic, pointed and conical instrument footprints and sampled footprint trails; it does not render dissolved swaths or solar-illumination masks. The explorer does not support observation scheduling, downlink latency, cost models or design-space optimization: say so plainly, offer what is supported, and never suggest tool calls with placeholder inputs. After an explorer error that user-supplied values cannot fix, stop and ask the user.

function.description:
Generate a satellite ground track over a time period. To show it on an
interactive map, use the ground track map tool instead.
function.name: generate_ground_track_mcp_tatc

duration.description:
How long to generate, e.g. "1 hour" or "60 minutes".
Defaults to 1 hour. Maximum 30 days and 2000 output points.

include_footprint.description:
Include footprint_geojson per point: the ground
area inside a 60 degree cone under the satellite, from TAT-C, as
a Polygon or a MultiPolygon split at the antimeridian. Defaults to
False: footprints are ~86% of the payload and tabular answers never
need them.

start_time.description:
Start time as ISO-8601, "now", or relative like "in one hour".
Defaults to "now".

step_interval.description:
Time step between points, e.g. "30 sec" or "1 minute".
Defaults to 1 minute. Between 1 second and 1 hour.

function.description:
Visualize, map, or plot a satellite ground track in the Cesium Study pane.

Opens a 2D map with 3D playback, sampled-position table and CSV export.
Without instrument, shows only the orbit and ground-track line: no sensor
coverage is inferred. Supply a researcher-agreed native TATC instrument to
draw dissolved sampled footprints using compute_ground_track. Basic sensors
require name and field_of_regard; pointed sensors add cross/along-track FOV;
conical sensors require name, cone_angle and along_track_field_of_view.
Never invent sensor geometry. Dissolved samples are not continuous coverage.
function.name: ground_track_map_mcp_tatc

dissolve_orbits.description: True combines the window; False keeps separate orbit groups.

duration.description: Defaults to 1 hour; positive and at most 30 days/2000 samples.

instrument.description: Optional explicit native TATC instrument JSON; no default cone.

satellite_identifier.description: Resolved satellite name or NORAD ID.

start_time.description: ISO-8601, now, or relative time; defaults to now.

step_interval.description: Defaults to 1 minute; from 1 second to 1 hour.

function.description:
Create an interactive research workspace; choose the output for the question.

This is not a keyword-triggered simulation tool. Use only when a visual or
interactive study is wanted. Do not call it for requests to write code, or
for text and numbers. Use conversation context; clarify only missing facts
that affect the result. A place and date alone are not a coverage study: ask
which satellites and sensors to use. Never invent measurements or sensor assumptions.
Not supported for point-coverage views: dissolved swath rendering, footprints of
basic field-of-regard instruments, solar-illumination masks, observation
scheduling/tasking, ground-station downlink/latency, cost models or
design-space optimization. Regional coverage uses the begin, region and finish
coverage workflow instead. Never invent TLEs, orbits or field of regard to approximate them.

presentation selects the initial view: overview for comparisons/charts,
timeline for observation and gap timing, table for exact values, map2d for
geographic context, simulation3d for orbital motion/spatial geometry. Charts
and tables do not load Cesium. All views share the same study pane and data.

view='data': dataset contains named numeric series aligned to labels, a common
unit, kind ('line' for a requested line chart, else 'bar') and provenance. Only
values the user typed (provenance kind 'user') or metrics of a coverage study
(kind 'study' with its analysis_id; labels are its point names) may be charted;
study values are checked. Source attribution is optional;
omit it when the prompt directly supplies the values. Use one data call for
such plots; no satellite lookup or coverage calculation is needed. Supports
overview (a labelled chart with axes) or table. Never invent values or sources.

view='coverage': supply the complete agreed scenario: TATC satellites with
explicit instruments (name and field_of_regard, or for a conical instrument
cone_angle and along_track_field_of_view; circular orbit fields: type, mean_altitude, inclination,
right_ascension_ascending_node, true_anomaly, epoch), study-point coordinates,
UTC start/end, and optional display_step_seconds. Supports all presentations; defaults to overview.
Missing mission or sensor inputs require clarification. Study-point coverage
is not regional coverage. Use analyze_coverage for numerical results alone.
To re-show an earlier study, pass its analysis_id instead of scenario.

view='ground_track': re-show or rerun a ground-track map with exactly one
satellite_identifiers entry, optional step_interval (1 second–1 hour),
start_time/duration (up to 30 days and 2000 samples), explicit instrument and
dissolve_orbits. No sensor geometry is assumed. Supports overview/table/map2d/simulation3d.

view='orbit': supply 1–4 resolved satellite identifiers. Optional start_time
defaults to now, duration to '1 hour', sampling to 60 seconds; report defaults.
Uses current CelesTrak GP elements. Supports altitude overview, sampled-position table,
map2d and simulation3d (default); no sensor or coverage is inferred.

view='example': explicitly requested hypothetical coverage example, with no
custom mission inputs; presentation may be selected. Never substitute it for
a user scenario. Coverage/example/orbit views are at most 24 hours/6000 display samples.
Explain limits and ask before changing the requested scope.
workspace_id is only for UI rerun intents, copied from their params; omit it otherwise.
function.name: visualize_mcp_tatc

kind.description: Required. 'line' for a line chart or run-ordered series, 'bar' for category comparisons.

analysis_id.description: The coverage study's analysis_id, for kind='study'.

provenance.description: Required. {'kind': 'user'} only when the user typed every value in this conversation; {'kind': 'study', 'analysis_id': ...} for metrics of a coverage study. Never chart invented, estimated or example values.

source.description: Optional source attribution, when known (for example a dataset or earlier analysis). Omit for values supplied directly in the prompt. Do not invent a citation or use the chart title as a source.

anyOf.description: Explicit scenario inputs shared by numerical and graphical tools.

display_step_seconds.description: 30–300 seconds. Orbit display sampling only; does not determine observation intervals.

end_time.description: ISO-8601 time; at most 24 hours after start.

items.description: A named WGS84 location; no area coverage is inferred between points.

satellites.description: 1–4 TATC Satellite JSON objects: name, orbit, and explicit instruments. Each instrument needs name and field_of_regard (degrees). A pointed instrument also has cross_track_field_of_view and along_track_field_of_view (degrees), and optional roll_angle, pitch_angle (degrees) and is_rectangular. A conical instrument has cone_angle and along_track_field_of_view (degrees) instead of field_of_regard, and optional scan_center_azimuth and scan_half_width (degrees); any instrument may set min_access_time (seconds), req_self_sunlit and req_target_sunlit (true for sunlit, false for eclipse). Supply an orbit type and epoch, an omm orbit with elements=[records] copied from the satellite info tool, or a tle orbit with both TLE lines from the user; element sets need an epoch within 30 days of the window. Hypothetical circular orbits use mean_altitude (meters), inclination (degrees), and optional right_ascension_ascending_node and true_anomaly (degrees).

start_time.description: ISO-8601 time with Z or a UTC offset.

function.description:
Analyze TATC observation opportunities and coverage gaps without opening a visual.

Use for numerical or informational coverage questions. Only use the coverage
view of the visualize tool instead when the request clearly implies visualization.

If the user has not supplied or agreed to satellites and sensor assumptions,
ask for them before calling. Never invent TLEs or instrument field of regard.
Not supported for point-coverage views: dissolved swath rendering, footprints of
basic field-of-regard instruments, solar-illumination masks, observation
scheduling/tasking, ground-station downlink/latency, cost models or
design-space optimization. Regional coverage uses the begin, region and finish
coverage workflow instead. Never invent TLEs, orbits or field of regard to approximate them.

Accepts a scenario with satellites (native TATC Satellite JSON), named points,
explicit start_time/end_time with UTC offsets, and optional display_step_seconds.
Supports hypothetical orbit designs, catalog orbits (type='omm',
elements=[records from the satellite info tool]) and supplied tle orbits
(type='tle', tle=[line1, line2]).
Each satellite must specify instruments with name and field_of_regard in degrees;
a conical instrument instead gives cone_angle and along_track_field_of_view, with
optional scan_center_azimuth and scan_half_width, in degrees.
A study with a pointed or conical instrument reports valid viewing epochs with
field-of-regard envelopes as metadata; its time covered, gaps and revisit are null.
A pointed instrument adds cross_track_field_of_view and along_track_field_of_view
(degrees) with optional roll_angle, pitch_angle and is_rectangular; any instrument
may set min_access_time (seconds), req_self_sunlit and req_target_sunlit.
For a circular orbit supply type='circular', mean_altitude in meters, inclination
in degrees, epoch with a UTC offset, and optional right_ascension_ascending_node
(RAAN) and true_anomaly in degrees; the names are exact. Points use name, latitude, longitude,
and optional WGS84 elevation in meters.

Limits: 4 satellites, 2 instruments each, 8 points, 24 hours, and 384
point-instrument-hours. Returns inputs, assumptions, individual observations,
merged coverage, gaps (including boundaries), and metrics. No area coverage is
inferred between points. Mean complete revisit excludes window boundaries and
is null when no complete gap exists. For visualization use the visualize tool with view=coverage
and the returned analysis_id. This computes opportunities, not executed tasks.
function.name: analyze_coverage_mcp_tatc

anyOf.description: Explicit scenario inputs shared by numerical and graphical tools.

display_step_seconds.description: 30–300 seconds. Orbit display sampling only; does not determine observation intervals.

end_time.description: ISO-8601 time; at most 24 hours after start.

items.description: A named WGS84 location; no area coverage is inferred between points.

satellites.description: 1–4 TATC Satellite JSON objects: name, orbit, and explicit instruments. Each instrument needs name and field_of_regard (degrees). A pointed instrument also has cross_track_field_of_view and along_track_field_of_view (degrees), and optional roll_angle, pitch_angle (degrees) and is_rectangular. A conical instrument has cone_angle and along_track_field_of_view (degrees) instead of field_of_regard, and optional scan_center_azimuth and scan_half_width (degrees); any instrument may set min_access_time (seconds), req_self_sunlit and req_target_sunlit (true for sunlit, false for eclipse). Supply an orbit type and epoch, an omm orbit with elements=[records] copied from the satellite info tool, or a tle orbit with both TLE lines from the user; element sets need an epoch within 30 days of the window. Hypothetical circular orbits use mean_altitude (meters), inclination (degrees), and optional right_ascension_ascending_node and true_anomaly (degrees).

start_time.description: ISO-8601 time with Z or a UTC offset.

function.description: Get satellite metadata and current GP (OMM) elements from CelesTrak.
function.name: get_satellite_info_mcp_tatc

function.description:
Search currently orbiting satellites by name in the CelesTrak database.

Decayed objects are excluded so returned names and NORAD IDs work with
the other tools. Use this first when the exact name is unknown.
function.name: search_satellites_mcp_tatc

limit.description: Maximum number of results, between 1 and 50. Defaults to 10.

function.description: Search the WMO OSCAR database for Earth observation instruments.
function.name: search_instruments_mcp_tatc

limit.description: Maximum number of results, between 1 and 50. Defaults to 10.

query.description: Instrument name, acronym, or partial name (e.g., "ABI", "MODIS").

function.description:
Get the instruments on a satellite, with OSCAR mission metadata.

Use this to build the instrument model input for observation or
coverage analysis. Resolves names and acronyms against the full OSCAR
satellite list; unknown or ambiguous names return an error.
function.name: get_satellite_instruments_mcp_tatc

satellite_identifier.description: Satellite acronym, name, or OSCAR slug.

function.description:
Get an OSCAR instrument record with measurement specs.

Resolves an instrument by acronym, name, or OSCAR slug. Spec fields
such as Resolution, Coverage / Cycle, and Scanning Technique are source
text from the OSCAR instrument page, not parsed numbers.
function.name: get_instrument_info_mcp_tatc

instrument_identifier.description: Instrument acronym, name, or OSCAR slug.

function.description:
Extract numeric candidates with provenance for assistant assessment.

Resolves an instrument by acronym, name, or OSCAR slug, then parses
numeric values from its specs and instrument descriptions. This tool
does not assess compatibility; read all returned context and provide a
geometry_assessment when finishing a run.
function.name: resolve_instrument_geometry_mcp_tatc

instrument_identifier.description: Instrument acronym, name, or OSCAR slug.

function.description:
Convert a ground swath width at an altitude to a field of regard.

Uses the same TAT-C math the generic coverage tool uses, so the
number matches the later run. Both inputs are flat numbers.
function.name: convert_swath_to_field_of_regard_mcp_tatc

orbit_altitude_m.description: Orbit altitude in meters, positive and finite.

swath_width_km.description: Ground swath width in km, positive and finite.

function.description:
Lock the satellites and UTC window for an access run.

Takes one satellite, or up to 6 separated by commas to model them
together as a constellation, e.g. "Sentinel-2A, Sentinel-2B".
Validates the inputs against current CelesTrak elements and returns
a draft ID with each satellite's orbit mean altitude. Set the region with the
region tool, then finish with grid size, geometry, and source. Start
must be an explicit UTC ISO-8601 value ending in Z or using +00:00.
End is the same format and defaults to 24 hours after the start when
omitted. The window is at most 366 days.
function.name: begin_access_run_mcp_tatc

end_time.description:
Exclusive UTC end, later than start_time. Defaults to
24 hours after start_time when omitted.

satellite_identifier.description:
Satellite name or NORAD ID for CelesTrak, or
up to 6 of them separated by commas.

function.description:
Set the region on a staged access draft.

Takes four separate numbers in west, south, east, north order; do
not nest them in a list. Longitude boxes must not cross the
antimeridian and must be narrower than 180 degrees. Returns the
draft with its region and the next step.
function.name: set_access_region_mcp_tatc

draft_id.description: Draft ID from the begin tool.

east_lon.description: Bounding-box east longitude, greater than west and at most 180.

north_lat.description: Bounding-box north latitude, greater than south and at most 90.

south_lat.description: Bounding-box south latitude, from -90 through less than 90.

west_lon.description: Bounding-box west longitude, from -180 through less than 180.

function.description:
Run a staged access analysis and save it under a result ID.

Takes a draft ID with its region already set, plus grid size, exactly
one of field of regard or swath width, a citation, and a structured
geometry_assessment. The assistant supplies its interpretation of the
complete source context. The server checks that the source_text includes
the selected number, but does not verify the interpretation. Understood
approximations run automatically and return their warning. Unclear or
conflicting evidence must be clarified first. Do not fetch the reference
URL. For a constellation, the same geometry applies to every satellite.
Set daylight_only
for optical imagers so night passes do not count. Works for any staged
window up to 366 days. A swath is converted at each satellite's orbit
altitude with TAT-C math. Modeled access does not confirm an acquisition.
function.name: finish_access_run_mcp_tatc

daylight_only.description:
Keep only accesses with the sun up at the cell
center, for optical imagers. Defaults to false.

draft_id.description: Draft ID from the begin tool.

field_of_regard_deg.description: Full cross-track angle in degrees, 0 to 360.

geometry_assessment.description:
Status, relevant source_text, explanation,
optional warning (required for approximate), and selected mode.

explanation.description: Why the selected number is supported or how the model approximates it.

mode.description: Selected source mode, when the source names one.

source_text.description: Relevant source evidence, including the selected geometry number.

status.description: Assistant assessment of this geometry for the coverage model.

warning.description: Required for approximate geometry; explain the model mismatch.

geometry_reference.description: Source for the angle or swath, required.

grid_columns.description: Number of equal longitude partitions, 1 through 12.

grid_rows.description: Number of equal latitude partitions, 1 through 12.

instrument_name.description: Label for the modeled scan. Defaults to modeled scan.

swath_width_km.description: Ground swath width in km as an alternative.

function.description:
Find reviewed shared instrument configuration revisions.

The lookup matches instrument, spacecraft name or alias, operating mode,
configuration ID, and revision. It returns identity, channel, applicability,
geometry, source evidence, geometry checks, source revision, interpretation,
approximations, source conflicts, and recorded source checks for each match.
It never chooses a configuration for a study. Pass the exact configuration
ID and revision returned here to the preparation tool.
function.name: lookup_instrument_configurations_mcp_tatc

instrument.description: Instrument name or part of its name.

operating_mode.description: Operating mode or part of its name.

revision.description: Exact immutable configuration revision, matched by equality.

function.description:
Record a source check supplied by the assistant or a maintainer.

This tool does not fetch source documents or edit the repository registry.
A changed geometry or applicability interval requires a complete sourced
configuration with a new immutable revision. The refresh record and candidate
remain in memory for this server process; a shared registry update requires a
reviewed repository change. A failed check records uncertainty and does not
claim that sources or geometry remain unchanged. Refresh state is capped at
256 records, 32 candidate revisions, and 1 MiB of serialized data. New checks
are rejected at capacity; existing notices are never evicted. Repeating an
identical check is idempotent, including equivalent UTC instants written with
other offsets. Source evidence for changed geometry or applicability must
exactly match the evidence retained in the updated configuration. A geometry
check may bind its reported value to a geometry parameter with
geometry_parameter. A revised geometry cannot keep a bound check that reports
the prior value, must cite the refresh evidence, and cannot silently remove
or narrow an approximation; removal requires evidence supporting
approximation.<id>.removed.
function.name: record_instrument_configuration_refresh_mcp_tatc

base_revision.description: Exact shared revision against which the source was checked.

checked_at_utc.description: UTC time when the source check was performed.

checked_source_revision_id.description: Source document revision or attempted check ID.

configuration_id.description: Stable ID of the reviewed shared configuration.

evidence_ids.description: Existing evidence IDs supporting this check.

failure_reason.description: Required explanation when status is failed.

function.description:
Prepare one sourced conical-scanning study without calculating.

Use this separate path for a conical scanner. Supply one complete
configuration with explicit units and reference frames, source evidence,
source revision, source conflicts and a chosen rationale, reported
geometry checks, applicability dates, and approximations, or select an
exact shared configuration ID and revision returned by the lookup tool.
The server validates the structure and values but does not authenticate
source text.
It returns the normalized proposal, region, grid, window, consequential
settings, warnings, and a setup revision. No TAT-C analysis runs yet.

The configuration describes one instrument on one spacecraft. Registry
lookup and explicit revision selection are supported, but multi-instrument
studies are not supported in this increment.
Cone angles, scan sector, velocity frame, nadir reference, and along-track
view are distinct from ground incidence and nominal swath width; do not
invent or silently convert them. Missing evidence, invalid units or
ranges, incompatible fields, unresolved source conflicts, failed checks,
unsupported model families, and windows outside the established
applicability interval are rejected before calculation.
function.name: prepare_conical_study_mcp_tatc

the researcher, and wait for their acceptance. Pass the proposal's exact

legacy field_of_regard_deg or swath_width_km arguments; use the legacy

Retrieve the full immutable setup for one draft or saved result.

Preparation, finish, and paged fetch responses are compact: they carry the
accepted setup revision, configuration digest, and a snapshot reference.

function.description:
Prepare one through six sourced conical or pointed configurations.

configurations must be a JSON list of objects. Each item is either an
exact registry selection with configuration_id and configuration_revision,
or a complete study-specific configuration nested as an object under
configuration; do not pass a JSON-encoded string. Each item may also carry
orbit_direction set to ascending or descending to keep only events on that
pass direction for that configuration. Every staged spacecraft
must have a selected configuration or a recorded omission. Preparation
checks established applicability and workload limits but runs no
viewing-event calculation. applicability_assumptions is an optional JSON
list of {configuration_id, start_utc, end_utc_exclusive, rationale}
entries that extend a selected configuration only when the researcher
explicitly accepts them.

omissions is an optional JSON list of requested instruments this study
cannot calculate. Each item names instrument and spacecraft plus an
optional mode and norad_id, a status of omitted or awaiting_clarification,
a reason_code of missing_evidence, unsupported_instrument,
unsupported_mode, unresolved_source_conflict, or other, and a reason;
awaiting entries also carry the question to resolve. Evidence entries may
carry authority, title, url, locator, excerpt, and note. A partial proposal
requires at least one calculable configuration.

The returned proposal preserves each identity, revision, source evidence,
orbit, geometry, illumination setting, and acceptance revision, plus every
omission and its reason. Accept the proposal before calling the mixed
finish tool; a partial proposal also requires accepting its exact omission
scope.
function.name: prepare_mixed_study_mcp_tatc

items.description: A researcher-accepted extension of a configuration's applicability.

One requested instrument this study cannot model.

Omitted entries are part of the accepted scope. An awaiting-clarification
entry records the open question without pretending the instrument is either
modeled or explicitly omitted. Mode comparison for duplicate detection is
exact text after trimming, so a descriptive alias does not match the
configuration's operating_mode.
A source reference retained with a requested-but-unmodeled instrument.

function.description:
Run only the current, explicitly accepted mixed study proposal.

When the proposal records omitted instruments, pass accepted_omissions
with exactly the omission IDs it returned, in addition to
accept_setup=true. An awaiting-clarification item must be resolved or
re-prepared as an explicit omission before the study can run.
function.name: finish_mixed_study_mcp_tatc

function.description:
Fetch paged conical viewing events by result ID.

Returns each valid TAT-C viewing epoch with its cell, satellite,
instrument, configuration identity, and broader field-of-regard envelope.
The envelope is metadata only; it is not continuous viewing time. Offset
starts at 0 and limit is 1 through 366. Every page includes the accepted
setup snapshot, provenance, warnings, and accounting definitions.
function.name: get_access_events_mcp_tatc

limit.description: Number of events to return, 1 through 366.

offset.description: Number of events to skip, 0 or more.

result_id.description: Result ID from a saved conical study.

function.description:
Fetch paged per-cell event-spacing values for a conical result.

Spacing is the difference between consecutive distinct viewing epochs at
the same cell, in hours. Fewer than two distinct events gives null
spacing. Simultaneous duplicate events count once. Each page includes the
accepted setup snapshot, provenance, warnings, and definitions.
function.name: get_access_event_spacing_mcp_tatc

limit.description: Number of cell rows to return, 1 through 366.

offset.description: Number of cell rows to skip, 0 or more.

result_id.description: Result ID from a saved conical study.

function.description:
Fetch saved daily observed and gap areas by result ID.

Pages through the daily rows of a saved access run without
re-running the analysis. Offset starts at 0 and limit is 1 to 366.
For conical studies, a cell counts on a UTC day only when a valid viewing
event epoch falls in that half-open day; envelope periods are not access.
function.name: get_access_daily_mcp_tatc

limit.description: Number of daily rows to return, 1 through 366.

offset.description: Number of daily rows to skip, 0 or more.

result_id.description: Result ID from a saved access run.

function.description:
Fetch the saved grid map by result ID as paged GeoJSON.

Returns grid cells as a GeoJSON feature collection, each cell marked
observed or gap for the saved window with its access count, mean
access minutes, and mean revisit hours. For conical studies, properties
report event counts, observed days, and event spacing instead; an observed
cell means only that at least one event epoch occurred at its center.
The collection metadata and feature properties retain geometry status and
warning. Filter with all, observed, or gaps. Offset starts at 0 and limit
is 1 through 366. Modeled access does not confirm an acquisition.
function.name: get_access_cells_mcp_tatc

include.description: Which cells to return: all, observed, or gaps.

limit.description: Number of matching cells to return, 1 through 366.

offset.description: Number of matching cells to skip, 0 or more.

function.description:
Fetch saved revisit numbers by result ID.

Returns mean, median, and max revisit hours, mean access minutes,
and the longest unobserved gap with their definitions, without
re-running the analysis. For conical studies this returns event-spacing
metrics instead and explicitly reports continuous viewing and uncovered
durations as unavailable. Modeled access does not confirm an acquisition.
function.name: get_access_revisit_mcp_tatc
